description: Pegged square with little wooden stakes, edges left ragged. Somebody began the tanning and gave up on it.
lore: Tanning is not difficult. It is only long: the same work, at the same hour, in the same place, for weeks — and the last part is what has gone out of this country. To peg a hide out is a promise that you will still be standing over this ground in a month, and the roads move and the fires go out. [[characters/7a779de1|Wendell]] remembers when a hide pegged in a yard meant nothing at all: that the yard would be there next month was not a thing anyone wondered about. So half-tanned squares come into the trade constantly, and are worth fourteen gold and a shrug. Except that the pegs are still in this one. It was lifted off the ground and rolled up with its stakes, which is not what you do with a job you have given up on. It is what you do with a job you mean to finish somewhere else.
gm_notes: The Drift measured in abandoned crafts: any trade needing a month in one place is dying out. The rolled pegs are the hopeful detail — whoever packed it still intended to finish.
